summary: Surge in 5xx rates after keepalive policy rollout causing upstream runtime restarts
description:
Issue summary:
A large customer (EchoHealth, dedicated pool) reported a sudden elevation in 5xx responses beginning ~2026-03-13 21:15 UTC after we rolled out an updated client keepalive policy in the us-east ingress tier. The elevated error rate correlates with increased connection churn on the API gateway and a series of short-lived upstream runtime worker restarts.

Impact:
- Customer-facing API requests returning 502/503/504 for ~18 minutes during the initial window.
- Elevated platform-wide errors for the affected us-east shard; multiple other tenants saw small blips.
- Streaming sessions experienced resets; long-lived streaming customers reported dropped sessions.

Environment:
- prod us-east (us-east-1) ingress fleet
- Dedicated runtime pool for EchoHealth (gpu pool: ded-echo-3)
- Keepalive policy change deployed via rollout group ingress-rollout-17 at 2026-03-13 21:00 UTC

Steps to reproduce / Observed pattern:
1) At 21:00 UTC the new keepalive policy (lower idle timeout, more aggressive connection close after 40s inactive) was enabled per rollout plan.
2) At ~21:15 UTC we observed a rapid spike in new connection resets from the API gateway to upstream proxies.
3) Connection churn increased accept-queue pressure on gateways and caused transient TLS handshake spikes.
4) Upstream runtimes reported short-lived worker process exits with GPU watchdog resets; NVML logs show driver soft-resets coincident with spikes.
5) Health checks caused ephemeral removal and re-add of workers, amplifying accept-queue pressure.

Logs / Metrics pointers:
- Grafana: dashboards/ingress/accept-queue-us-east (sharp rise at 21:12 UTC)
- Sentry: runtime/worker-watchdog (several SIGTERM/SIGABRT events around 21:14-21:20)
- ELB/NGINX logs: repeated FIN/RST between apigw-pool-17 and proxy nodes
- NVML driver logs: /var/log/nvidia/nvml-rolls.log -> multiple soft-resets during window

Expected behavior:
- Keepalive policy rollout should not cause systemic connection churn causing upstream worker restarts. Runtimes should handle transient socket closes gracefully and maintain steady accept queues.

Attachments:
- sample apigw access logs (attached)

investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: The aggressive keepalive policy reduced idle socket lifetime causing higher churn of short-lived TCP/TLS sessions. This increased the ingress accept/handshake rate, saturating proxy CPU and causing TLS worker thread stalls. Stalled threads prevented graceful draining of GPU requests; GPU watchdogs triggered soft-resets on a subset of runtimes (observed via NVML). The combination created a feedback loop: restarts -> health-check-driven rebalances -> more accept-queue pressure.

Findings:
- Timeline aligns with rollout start + error spike.
- NVML logs show clustered soft-resets on three worker processes in ded-echo-3 pool.
- Apigw CPU and accept-queue metrics show >3x baseline during window.
- No prior configuration change on runtimes at that time.

Partial reproduction steps used in lab:
- Simulated aggressive client keepalive behavior against a staging apigw cluster with limited proxy capacity; reproduced accept-queue growth and TLS handshake spike.

Mitigation attempted:
- Immediate: Disabled the new keepalive policy for us-east; paused rollout globally.
- Short term: Added accept-queue backpressure thresholds and tuned proxy thread pools to increase handshake capacity.
- Long term: plan to add jittered keepalive transition, increase proxy handshaker throughput during rollouts, and adjust healthcheck sensitivity to avoid amplifying transient restarts.
resolution:
Mitigations applied 2026-03-13 21:50 UTC: rollout paused and keepalive policy reverted for us-east. Error rates returned to baseline by 22:00 UTC.

Root cause: Keepalive idle-time reduction combined with our current proxy threading and healthcheck thresholds created a connection-thrashing -> worker restart feedback loop. The runtime GPU watchdogs were firing due to brief periods of scheduling starvation coincident with heavy TLS handshake CPU.

Fixes completed / next steps:
1) Reverted keepalive change for affected region (done).
2) Hotfix: increased apigw handshaker thread pool and tuned TLS backlog timeout to reduce handshake stalls (deployed 2026-03-13 21:55 UTC).
3) Runtime follow-up: schedule patch to stagger healthcheck grace windows and add cooldown after soft-resets to avoid immediate re-add (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2248).
4) Postmortem: Owner assigned (Diego Martinez). Postmortem to include rollout playbook updates, target date 2026-03-18.
5) Customer outreach: sent timeline and workaround to EchoHealth CSM; offered a dedicated incident review call.

Status: Customer impact resolved; monitoring enabled. Follow-ups in backlog: adjust rollout runner to apply jitter/gradual connection policy, unit test for keepalive vs proxy capacity, and update runbook for keepalive rollouts.
notes_for_postmortem:
- Add a simulation step to rollout pipeline that mimics aggressive client keepalive churn against a representative ingress size.
- Re-evaluate healthcheck removal/add thresholds to avoid immediate rebalancing after soft resets.
- Add telemetry: a short-time sliding window metric for TLS handshake rate and NVML soft-reset counts correlated by node to detect early signs.
- Update customer communication templates for keepalive-related incidents.
